subject: color or carve out (non-solid) scale_size points

messages.author: 08f3062efe0fd1ca
messages.subject: color or carve out (non-solid) scale_size points
parts:
Hello List,

is there a way to color points that were drawn with size (geom_point(aes(size=st_zir_kat)))? Alternatively, I would like to make points "hollow". I would basically want a differently sized circles on my plot. I have tried scale_shape(solid=FALSE), but no dice. I get a lot of overlap and would like to present my data more clearly. Here is my code:

zir_bp <- qplot(obs_b, nmv, data=zir) #tree circumference on x, altitude on y and number of beech masts as size
st_zir_kat <- cut(st_zir_0.1, breaks=c(0,1,50,100,500), labels=c("0", "50", "100", "500"))
    zir_bp +
        geom_point(aes(size=st_zir_kat)) +
        scale_size_manual(values=c(2, 5, 10, 15, 20), "Št. žirov") +
        xlab("Obseg bukve [m]") +
        scale_shape(solid=FALSE) +
        ylab("Nadmorska višina [m]")

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: cd9baedf48d871eb
messages.subject: Re: color or carve out (non-solid) scale_size points
parts:
Hi,

Hadley's book has a part dealing with overplotting. See section 5.5
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/book/

Basically, you might want to use a different geom or use transparency,
for example.

Anyway, was your first question: how to use both size and colour
scales, with the same variable? If I understood correctly, then the
answer is:
zir_bp + geom_point(aes(size=st_zir_kat, colour=st_zir_kat)) +

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: color or carve out (non-solid) scale_size points
parts:
You might want to try manually specifying the shape:

geom_point(aes(size=st_zir_kat), shape = 1)

Hadley
